title: Work piles up when it arrives faster than the workers finish
try: change "workers 3" to "workers 2", or click a worker to kill it.
summary: A queue, workers and a retry loop. One worker fewer and the line never stops growing.

title: One shared line beats one line per worker
try: watch the chart. Both rows have the same work and the same four workers. Then click a worker in each row to kill it.
summary: Same load, same workers, different lines. The chart shows the wait each row gets.

title: Retries keep a system down after the spike has gone
try: wait for the burst at 15 seconds. Then change "copy after 5s" to "after 5s" and press restart.
summary: Clients give up and try again, but the abandoned work still gets done. Gray tokens are work nobody wants.

title: Empty the cache and the database falls behind
try: click the cache, then press "empty the cache". The database only ever coped because the cache hid most of the work.
summary: A cache that earns its hit rate from what it remembers. Popular items come up most.

title: Fan-out makes rare slowness common
try: click split, then press compare on "split 8". One slow part in fifty is enough once a job waits for many.
summary: One job becomes many, and it finishes when the slowest part does.

title: Taking turns keeps feeding a dead worker
try: click every box in one row to kill that worker. Then change "round robin" to "least busy".
summary: A load balancer with three workers. How it chooses decides what a failure costs.

title: Batches too small back up, and batches too big wait for nothing
try: click batch, then press compare on the 4. There is a best size, and it isn't the biggest.
summary: A worker does a whole batch in the time of one job, so batching buys capacity and costs waiting.

title: A priority lane lets other work wait forever
try: watch the two chart lines split apart. Then delete "priority gold" from the queue's label.
summary: Named work takes the front of the line. The chart shows what that costs everything else.

title: A rate limit keeps the line short by saying no
try: click the rate limit and press compare on the 3, or delete its label to see what it was holding back.
summary: Too much work arrives. Without a limit the wait grows without end. With one, the cost moves to work turned away.

title: A circuit breaker stops calling a service that keeps failing
try: press 1 three times to trip it, then wait five seconds.
summary: A state machine: its arrows are the events and timers it obeys.

title: Waiting twice as long after each failure gives a service room to recover
try: press fail again and again. The wait doubles each time, then it gives up.
summary: Guards, counters and actions, written on arrows the way a state diagram writes them.

title: Where you start stops mattering
try: drag the start arrow onto rainy. The bars end up in the same place.
summary: A chance walk with 300 walkers. Each black tick is where that shape settles in the long run.

title: Two gates that feed each other remember
try: turn "set" on and off. The lamp stays lit. Then turn "reset" on and off.
summary: The smallest memory there is. Changes travel along wires at a speed you can see.

title: Chained flip-flops count in binary
try: watch the lamps count up. Each one runs at half the speed of the one before.
summary: A clock and four flip-flops. Delete a wire and the higher bits stop.
